citeAs: Helber, P., Bischke, B., Dengel, A., & Borth, D. (2018). Introducing EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. 2018 IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (IGARSS).
creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth (TU Kaiserslautern; German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI))
description: EuroSAT is a land use and land cover classification dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images. It contains 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced image patches across 10 classes and covers 13 spectral bands, with RGB and multi-spectral versions released.
name: EuroSAT
publisher: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports manual validation rather than formal inter-annotator metrics: all 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times, and the ground truth was corrected by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset was created from Sentinel-2A image patches associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas. The 27,000 image patches were labeled and manually checked multiple times, and the ground truth was corrected by sorting out mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice.
rai:dataBiases: To reduce narrow geographic and seasonal bias, the authors aimed to cover as many countries as possible across Europe and extracted images recorded all over the year to increase intra-class variance. The dataset is nevertheless limited to European cities associated with the European Urban Atlas, and the class distribution is influenced by the number of represented cities per country in that atlas.
rai:dataCollection: The authors downloaded Sentinel-2A satellite images via Amazon S3, choosing images associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas across 34 European countries. They selected scenes with low cloud level and then created 27,000 geo-referenced 64x64 image patches labeled into 10 land use and land cover classes.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: To improve the chance of getting valuable image patches, the authors selected satellite images with a low cloud level using ESA's cloud level metadata. During manual checking they also sorted out mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of multi-spectral Sentinel-2A satellite images from the Copernicus program, acquired over cities covered by the European Urban Atlas. The source imagery covers 13 spectral bands, and patches were extracted from these satellite scenes.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Images were extracted from Sentinel-2A scenes and recorded all over the year; the paper does not provide exact start and end dates for dataset collection.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is designed around classes that are visible at 10 meters per pixel and frequently covered by the European Urban Atlas, so it does not cover finer-grained classes requiring higher spatial resolution. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with color cast, and a patch-based classifier trained on 64x64 images does not allow finely graduated per-pixel segmentation.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors extracted 64x64 image patches from Sentinel-2 scenes, released both RGB and multi-spectral versions, sorted out mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice, and retained some samples with atmospheric color cast rather than filtering them out so the classifier could learn these cases. For band evaluation, lower-resolution bands were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were selected with low cloud level, patches of size 64x64 were extracted, and all 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times to correct labels and remove patches that were mislabeled or full of snow or ice. The dataset was released in RGB and multi-spectral forms; for some experiments, lower-resolution bands were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that the dataset and resulting classification system can support Earth observation applications such as agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change, urban development, environmental monitoring, land use and land cover change detection, nature protection, sustainable development, and improving geographical maps.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended use cases include land use and land cover classification, large-scale training of deep neural networks for satellite image classification, land use and land cover change detection, monitoring Earth’s land surface, and assisting in keeping geographical maps such as OpenStreetMap up to date.
